module.title: Unit 7: Remote Working vs. Office Life: The Future of Work
module.objective: Mampu menyusun opini berimbang tentang model kerja remote versus kantor menggunakan concession clauses (although, even though).

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Finding the Right Place to Work
subModules.grammarFocus: Concession clauses with although and even though
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Work arrangements, teamwork, productivity, and work-life balance

content.summary: Read about two employees who compare working from home with working in an office. You will identify the main ideas and details, learn useful work vocabulary, and see how although and even though help writers present a balanced opinion.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use although and even though to recognize a contrast between an accepted fact and the writer's main point. Either clause can come first.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn words for flexible schedules, teamwork, feelings of isolation, productivity, hybrid work, and personal life.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the passage first to find its main idea. Then scan for details about each worker's routine, benefits, and problems.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a B1 text comparing remote and office work.
Locate details about employees' schedules, teamwork, and work-life balance.
Recognize how although and even though introduce a contrast.
Use context to understand key vocabulary about modern work.

contextWarmup.prompt: Which work arrangement might suit someone who needs quiet time to concentrate but also enjoys meeting colleagues?
options: A hybrid model
Working in a busy office every day
Working alone without meeting anyone
contextWarmup.explanation: A hybrid model can give someone quiet time at home and opportunities to meet colleagues at the office.

rules: Use although followed by a subject and verb to introduce a fact that contrasts with your main point: Although home working saves travel time, it can feel lonely.
Even though has the same basic pattern as although, but it often gives the contrast stronger emphasis: Even though the office is noisy, Sam works well there.
You can put the main clause first. Do not use but in the same clause with although or even though: Remote work is useful, although it is not right for everyone.

commonTrap.explanation: Do not add but to a sentence that already begins with although or even though. The two words both show a contrast, so using both in the same sentence is unnecessary.
commonTrap.wrong: Although remote work saves time, but some people miss their colleagues.
commonTrap.correct: Although remote work saves time, some people miss their colleagues.

paragraphs: Maya and Leo work for the same small design company, but they prefer different routines. Maya works from home most days. She likes the flexibility because she can begin early and take a proper break at lunchtime. Her commute used to take an hour each way, so working at home gives her more time for family and exercise.

Leo goes to the office four days a week. He enjoys quick conversations with colleagues and says collaboration is easier when everyone can look at the same designs. Although the office can be noisy, he finds it easier to focus there than at home. Maya sometimes feels isolation after long days alone, while Leo occasionally finds the commute tiring.

Their manager has introduced a hybrid model. The team now meets in the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays, then chooses where to work on other days. Even though Maya values working at home, she likes meeting the team in person. Leo uses his home days for tasks that need quiet. They have not found one perfect system, but both say their productivity has improved.

The arrangement also helps them think about work-life balance. Maya plans her hours carefully so that work does not take over her evenings. Leo likes having a clear end to his office day, even though he still checks messages sometimes. Their experience shows that the best choice can depend on a person's job, home, and habits.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: A Balanced View of Work

content.summary: Write a balanced opinion about remote work and office life. Use although or even though to recognise a different point before giving your main argument. You can also put the main argument first and add the contrasting point at the end.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Recognise a Different Point
blueprintItems.formula: Although + subject + verb, subject + verb + main opinion.
blueprintItems.example: Although remote work saves travel time, some employees miss talking to their colleagues.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Emphasise a Strong Contrast
blueprintItems.formula: Even though + subject + verb, subject + verb + main opinion.
blueprintItems.example: Even though the office is noisy, it can help some people focus on their work.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Put Your Main Opinion First
blueprintItems.formula: Main opinion + although/even though + subject + verb.
blueprintItems.example: Many workers prefer the office, although working from home gives them more flexibility.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma after an although or even though clause when it comes first.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Although remote work saves time many workers miss their teams.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Although remote work saves time, many workers miss their teams.
mechanicsRules.why: The comma separates the opening contrast from the main opinion.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not use a comma before although or even though when the contrasting clause comes at the end of the sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Office workers can share ideas, although remote workers can share ideas online.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Office workers can share ideas although remote workers can share ideas online.
mechanicsRules.why: The contrast comes after the main opinion, so a comma is not usually needed in this sentence.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a subject and a verb in both parts of an although or even though sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Although working from home, some people feel lonely.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Although some people enjoy working from home, they can feel lonely.
mechanicsRules.why: In this pattern, each clause needs a subject and a verb.

reading.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Different people can benefit from different work arrangements.
Everyone should work from home every day.
Office work is always more productive.
reading.answer: Different people can benefit from different work arrangements.
reading.explanation: Maya and Leo prefer different routines, and the hybrid arrangement helps each of them.

reading.question: Why does Maya like working from home?
options: It gives her more flexibility and saves commuting time.
She never has to speak to her colleagues.
Her manager requires her to work late.
reading.answer: It gives her more flexibility and saves commuting time.
reading.explanation: The first paragraph says she can choose an early start and gets time back because she no longer commutes every day.

reading.question: How many days a week does Leo usually go to the office?
options: Two days
Four days
Five days
reading.explanation: The passage states that Leo goes to the office four days a week.

reading.question: Why does Leo find collaboration easier at the office?
options: Everyone can look at the same designs together.
The office is always quiet.
He does not have any design tasks at home.
reading.answer: Everyone can look at the same designs together.
reading.explanation: Leo says that collaboration is easier when the team can look at the same designs.

reading.question: What does Maya sometimes feel after long days alone?
options: Isolation
Excitement
Boredom with her job
reading.explanation: The second paragraph says Maya sometimes feels isolation after long days alone.

reading.question: When does the team meet at the office under the hybrid model?
options: On Tuesdays and Thursdays
Every Monday
Only at the end of the month
reading.explanation: The manager asks the team to meet in the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

reading.question: What does Leo do on his home-working days?
options: He works on tasks that need quiet.
He meets the team in person.
He takes the day off.
reading.answer: He works on tasks that need quiet.
reading.explanation: The third paragraph explains that Leo uses his home days for quiet tasks.

reading.question: What does although show in the sentence about the noisy office?
options: A contrast between the office being noisy and Leo focusing well there.
A reason that Leo never visits the office.
A sequence of two events.
reading.answer: A contrast between the office being noisy and Leo focusing well there.
reading.explanation: Although introduces the fact that the office can be noisy, before contrasting it with Leo's ability to focus there.

reading.question: What does Maya do to protect her work-life balance?
options: She plans her hours so work does not take over her evenings.
She works in the office every evening.
She stops meeting her colleagues.
reading.answer: She plans her hours so work does not take over her evenings.
reading.explanation: The final paragraph says Maya plans her hours carefully to protect her evenings.

reading.question: Which statement best describes the writer's view of remote and office work?
options: The best choice depends on the person's job, home, and habits.
Remote work is the best choice for every employee.
A hybrid model never works well.
reading.answer: The best choice depends on the person's job, home, and habits.
reading.explanation: The passage ends by saying that the best choice can depend on a person's job, home, and habits.

reading.question: What is the primary function of the modal verb in 'You ought to back up your database before the migration'?
options: Strong moral or practical recommendation
Logical certainty
Physical capability
Past habit
reading.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses a strong advisory recommendation or obligation.

reading.question: Which word best replaces 'alleviate' in 'measures were introduced to alleviate employee stress'?
options: Reduce
Intensify
Ignore
Prolong
reading.explanation: 'Alleviate' means to make a problem or burden less severe.

reading.question: In professional correspondence, which salutation and sign-off pair is the most appropriate for a formal inquiry?
options: Dear Mr. Harrison / Sincerely yours
Hey buddy / Cheers
To whom it concerns / Talk soon
Good morning friend / Bye for now
reading.explanation: Formal business register requires respectful titles and conventional complimentary closes.

reading.question: Select the sentence with the correct non-defining relative clause punctuation:
options: Our senior analyst, who joined the firm last January, presented the financial forecast.
Our senior analyst who joined the firm last January presented the financial forecast.
Our senior analyst, who joined the firm last January presented the financial forecast.
Our senior analyst who joined the firm last January, presented the financial forecast.
reading.answer: Our senior analyst, who joined the firm last January, presented the financial forecast.
reading.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses must be enclosed by commas on both sides.

reading.question: What does the expression 'think outside the box' convey in an entrepreneurial context?
options: Approach problems with non-traditional and creative perspectives.
Store physical inventory outside the warehouse boundaries.
Follow standard operating procedures without deviation.
Ignore financial accounting standards during quarterly audits.
reading.answer: Approach problems with non-traditional and creative perspectives.
reading.explanation: The idiom 'think outside the box' signifies lateral and innovative thinking.

writing.instruction: Join the two ideas using although. Put the although clause first.
writing.promptText: Remote work offers flexibility. Some workers miss their colleagues.
writing.hint: Start with Although and put a comma between the two clauses.
targetAnswers: Although remote work offers flexibility, some workers miss their colleagues.
writing.explanation: Although introduces the contrasting fact. Use a comma when this clause comes first.

writing.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with even though at the beginning.
writing.promptText: The office is noisy, but some employees work well there.
writing.hint: Put the noisy office fact after Even though.
targetAnswers: Even though the office is noisy, some employees work well there.
writing.explanation: Even though introduces the strong contrast, and the main opinion follows the comma.

writing.instruction: Move the although clause to the end of the sentence.
writing.promptText: Although video meetings are convenient, some people prefer meeting in person.
writing.hint: Begin with the main opinion and finish with the although clause.
targetAnswers: Some people prefer meeting in person although video meetings are convenient.
writing.explanation: The main clause can come first. A comma is not usually needed before an although clause at the end.

writing.instruction: Complete the sentence with although or even though.
writing.promptText: _____ working from home is very convenient, I sometimes feel lonely.
writing.hint: Both choices can show contrast. Use even though to give the contrast more emphasis.
targetAnswers: Even though working from home is very convenient, I sometimes feel lonely.
Although working from home is very convenient, I sometimes feel lonely.
writing.explanation: Both conjunctions are possible. Even though gives stronger emphasis to the contrast.

writing.instruction: Choose the best conjunction to complete the sentence.
writing.promptText: _____ not every job can be done remotely, many companies offer employees flexible work options.
writing.hint: Choose a word that introduces a contrast.
targetAnswers: Although not every job can be done remotely, many companies offer employees flexible work options.
writing.explanation: Although introduces the fact that some jobs cannot be done remotely before the main point.

writing.instruction: Correct the capitalization, punctuation, and verb form.
writing.promptText: even though the office have a quiet room many workers prefer home
writing.hint: Start with a capital letter, use has with the office, and add a comma after the opening clause.
targetAnswers: Even though the office has a quiet room, many workers prefer home.
writing.explanation: The office is singular, so use has. Add a comma after the opening even though clause and a full stop at the end.

writing.instruction: Correct the punctuation in this sentence.
writing.promptText: I like working at home, although I miss talking to my team.
writing.hint: The although clause comes at the end of the sentence.
targetAnswers: I like working at home although I miss talking to my team.
writing.explanation: A comma is not usually needed before an although clause at the end of this sentence.

writing.instruction: Correct the sentence using although and a complete clause.
writing.promptText: Although working in an office, some people prefer it.
writing.hint: Add a subject and verb after although.
targetAnswers: Although some people can work from home, they prefer the office.
writing.explanation: The although clause needs a subject and a verb. The corrected sentence also clearly shows the contrast.

writing.instruction: Write one balanced sentence about remote work using although.
writing.promptText: Include one advantage of remote work and one different point.
writing.hint: For example, recognise the flexibility before saying what some workers find difficult.
targetAnswers: Although remote work offers flexibility, some workers find it difficult to separate work and home life.
Although remote work saves travel time, some people miss face-to-face contact.
writing.explanation: A suitable answer recognises one point and then gives a contrasting main idea. Other clear answers are possible.

writing.instruction: Write two sentences giving a balanced opinion about office work and remote work. Use even though in one sentence.
writing.promptText: Include one reason to work in an office and one reason to work remotely.
writing.hint: Use even though to recognise a strong contrasting point, then state your main opinion.
targetAnswers: Even though the office can be noisy, it helps me share ideas with my team. Remote work saves time, so I prefer a mix of both.
Even though remote work is flexible, I like the office because I can talk to my colleagues easily. Both settings have advantages.
writing.explanation: A good response gives a clear opinion, mentions both work settings, and uses even though to show a contrast.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the two ideas using although. Put the although clause first.

targetAnswers: Although remote work offers flexibility, some workers miss their colleagues.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Although introduces the contrasting fact. Use a comma when this clause comes first.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with even though at the beginning.

practicumQuestions.hint: Put the noisy office fact after Even though.
targetAnswers: Even though the office is noisy, some employees work well there.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Even though introduces the strong contrast, and the main opinion follows the comma.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Move the although clause to the end of the sentence.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Although video meetings are convenient, some people prefer meeting in person.

practicumQuestions.explanation: The main clause can come first. A comma is not usually needed before an although clause at the end.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Both conjunctions are possible. Even though gives stronger emphasis to the contrast.

targetAnswers: Even though the office has a quiet room, many workers prefer home.
